# Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 frames). No separate IDS/alert export was present in the evidence directory; findings below are derived directly from the pcap via tshark.

**Capture window:** 2024-07-30 06:38:48 to 06:48:34 (UTC+4), ~9.75 minutes.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.16.1.66** |
| MAC address | **00:1e:64:ec:f3:08** (Intel NIC vendor) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** |
| Logged-in Windows user | **ccollier** (confirmed independently via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString `ccollier`, and via the malware's own C2 check-in field) |
| Windows domain | wiresharkworkshop.online (AD domain; DC = 172.16.1.4, `WIRESHARK-WS-DC`) |
| OS (self-reported by malware) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit |

## Malware family

**StrRAT** — **signature-confirmed**, not behavioral inference. The C2 check-in traffic contains the literal ASCII string `STRRAT` and the malware's own version tag `1.6` inside its plaintext, pipe-delimited beacon protocol (see raw payload below). StrRAT is a Java-based RAT distributed via malspam/fake-installer campaigns; its hallmark is this exact `ping|STRRAT|<campaignID>|<hostname>|<user>|<OS>|<arch>|<AV>||<version>|<country>|<status>|<uptime>` heartbeat format, observed here verbatim.

Sample decoded beacon (TCP stream 83, repeated every ~5 seconds for the life of the capture):

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

- Campaign/build ID: `1BE8292C`
- Reported AV product: Windows Defender
- Reported persistence status: "Not Installed"
- No commands other than `ping` heartbeats were observed in the captured window — no evidence in this pcap of file exfiltration, keylogging, or additional payload retrieval by the operator during the capture.

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — StrRAT C2 server, raw TCP (no TLS), plaintext protocol. Contacted directly by IP; no DNS lookup for this host was observed, i.e. the C2 address is hardcoded in the sample. Beaconing began at capture-relative time ~77s and continued for the remainder of the capture (~508s), one persistent TCP stream (tcp.stream 83), source port 49754 → destination port 12132.

**Malicious domains:** None observed. The C2 channel uses a bare IP address with no accompanying DNS resolution, so no malicious domain can be grounded in this traffic.

**Malicious URLs:** None observed. No HTTP request in the capture carries a StrRAT-related path; the only plaintext HTTP requests seen are a legitimate Windows connectivity check (`http://www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt`) and a geolocation lookup (`http://ip-api.com/json/`, likely triggered by the malware or a companion process to fingerprint the victim's public IP/location — response shows Austin, TX, Google Fiber, IP 136.49.34.127).

**Transferred files / hashes:** None recoverable. No executable, JAR, or other payload transfer was captured (HTTP object export yielded only `connecttest.txt` and the ip-api JSON response; SMB traffic in the capture is limited to routine Group Policy file reads from the domain controller). The infection vector and initial payload delivery therefore fall outside this capture's window — only the post-infection C2 beacon is present. No SHA256 hash can be computed from this evidence.

## Summary

Host 172.16.1.66 (DESKTOP-SKBR25F, user ccollier) is compromised with **StrRAT v1.6** (build/campaign `1BE8292C`), confirmed by its distinctive plaintext C2 heartbeat protocol observed live in the capture. The malware beacons every ~5 seconds to **141.98.10.79:12132** over plain TCP. No lateral movement, data exfiltration, or secondary payload activity is visible in this capture; all other traffic from the host (AD/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB to the domain controller, Microsoft/Bing/MSN telemetry, GitHub, Maven Central, Oracle Java update check) is consistent with normal enterprise workstation and background-process behavior and is not evidence of additional compromise.

**Recommended action:** Isolate 172.16.1.66 from the network, block 141.98.10.79:12132 at the perimeter, force a credential reset for ccollier and any accounts used on this host, and perform full disk/memory forensics to recover the initial infection vector and dropped StrRAT JAR/loader, since neither is present in this pcap.
